cards.title: How rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) panels generate clean power
facts: Solar photovoltaic (PV) cells contain semiconductor silicon that knocks electrons free when struck by sunlight.
Rooftop solar generates zero carbon emissions during operation, replacing polluting thermal coal power.
do: Understand that rooftop solar panels convert sunlight directly into direct current (DC) electricity
An inverter converts DC into alternating current (AC) to power household fans, lights, and computers
Net-metering allows excess solar power generated during sunny afternoons to be exported back to the city grid
dont: Never walk or jump on solar glass panels (cracks micro-silicon cells and destroys efficiency)
Never let thick layers of dust or bird droppings accumulate on panels (wash with clean water)

myths.statement: Solar panels only work on boiling hot summer days and stop producing electricity in winter.
myths.truth: Solar panels operate on SUNLIGHT (photons), not heat. In fact, solar cells operate more efficiently in cool, sunny winter air.

quiz.q: What device in a rooftop solar setup converts Direct Current (DC) from panels into Alternating Current (AC) for home appliances?
quiz.explanation: The solar inverter converts DC generated by silicon cells into 230V AC used by household appliances.

situations: {name}'s school or home at {at} is installing a 5-kilowatt rooftop solar system.
scenario.question: What clean energy principles should {name} explain?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Rooftop silicon panels convert sunlight photons directly into clean electricity with zero emissions
The solar inverter transforms DC into AC, and net-metering exports surplus power to the grid
Keep panels clean from dust and bird droppings with periodic water washing

sources.name: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (PM Surya Ghar Scheme)

cards.title: Electric vehicles (EVs): Tailpipe emissions and regenerative braking
facts: Electric vehicles produce zero tailpipe emissions, eliminating street-level lung-damaging NO2 and PM2.5.
Regenerative braking reverses electric motors during deceleration, capturing kinetic energy back into the battery.
do: Understand that electric scooters and cars use high-efficiency electric motors powered by lithium-ion battery packs
Charge EVs using designated charging equipment and avoid using ungrounded makeshift extension cords
Advocate for electric public transit (electric city buses and metro rail) to slash citywide air pollution
dont: Never leave EV battery chargers exposed to heavy rain without weatherproof protection
Never use damaged, cracked, or punctured lithium battery packs

myths.statement: Electric vehicles cause identical street pollution as petrol cars because batteries burn fuel.
myths.truth: EVs have zero tailpipe emissions; they produce zero toxic exhaust on city streets where children walk and breathe.

quiz.q: What smart technology in electric vehicles recovers energy when the driver applies brakes?
options: Regenerative braking (converts kinetic stopping energy into stored battery charge)
quiz.explanation: Regenerative braking turns the motor into a generator, recharging batteries during slowing down.

situations: A family at {at} is deciding between buying a petrol scooter or an electric scooter.
scenario.question: What green tech benefits should {name} highlight?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Electric scooters have zero tailpipe emissions, keeping city street air clean for pedestrians
rubric.keys: zero tailpipe emissions|clean air|no petrol smoke

rubric.point: EVs have significantly lower running and maintenance costs per kilometer compared to petrol
rubric.keys: lower running cost|cheaper per km|low maintenance

rubric.point: Charge safely using certified wall chargers with proper electrical earthing

dangerous: charge ev with damaged ungrounded wire

sources.name: NITI Aayog (Shoonya - Zero Pollution Mobility Campaign)

cards.title: BEE Star Energy Rating labels: Saving units and money
facts: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) rates household appliances from 1 Star (least efficient) to 5 Stars (most efficient).
A 5-Star inverter air conditioner consumes up to 30% less electricity than a 1-Star model over its lifetime.
do: Look for the official red-and-white BEE Star Label when buying appliances (refrigerators, ACs, fans, geysers)
Compare the 'Units / Year' (kWh) figure on the label to calculate actual annual electricity savings
Encourage family to choose 5-Star rated appliances: higher star rating means lower electricity bills and lower coal burned
dont: Never peel off or ignore BEE energy efficiency labels on home appliances
Never buy uncertified electrical appliances without genuine BEE rating logos

myths.statement: A 1-Star rated air conditioner cools the room much faster and stronger than a 5-Star rated model.
myths.truth: Star ratings measure energy efficiency, not cooling power. A 5-Star AC cools identically while using significantly less electricity.

quiz.q: What does a 5-Star rating on a Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) label indicate?
options: Maximum energy efficiency: consumes the lowest electricity to deliver the same performance
quiz.explanation: Higher star ratings denote superior technological efficiency and lower electricity consumption.

situations: Shopping for a new family refrigerator or ceiling fan at {at}, the salesperson points to different models.
scenario.question: How should {name} help the family choose wisely?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Check the BEE Star Rating label and select a high-efficiency 5-Star rated model
rubric.note: Minimizes daily electricity consumption and utility costs.
rubric.keys: bee star label|5 star rating|energy efficiency|lower electricity

rubric.point: Explain that higher initial cost is recovered within 1-2 years through significantly lower power bills
Verify the official BEE logo and annual electricity consumption figure on the label

cards.title: Lighting efficiency: Why LEDs beat incandescent and CFL bulbs
facts: Old incandescent bulbs waste 90% of electricity as useless heat, converting only 10% into light.
Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) consume 80% less power than incandescent bulbs and last over 25,000 hours.
do: Replace remaining incandescent yellow bulbs and fluorescent tubes with high-efficiency LED lights
Switch off lights and fans every time you leave an empty room ('The Last Person Out Rule')
Clean dust off LED light covers periodically to maximize brightness without increasing wattage
dont: Never leave room lights burning in broad daylight with curtains open
Never dispose of old mercury-containing CFL tubes in household wet trash

myths.statement: Old yellow incandescent bulbs are much healthier for study rooms than modern energy-efficient LEDs.
myths.truth: Incandescent bulbs waste 90% of power as heat and burn out quickly. Warm LEDs provide superior study lighting with 80% less power.

quiz.q: What percentage of electricity did old-fashioned filament light bulbs waste as useless heat?
options: Approximately 90% wasted as heat, producing only 10% light
quiz.explanation: Filament bulbs operate by thermal incandescence, wasting nearly all energy as radiated heat.

situations: Replacing old lighting fixtures at home or school at {at}, {name} evaluates different bulb types.
scenario.question: What green technology facts should {name} present?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Install energy-efficient LED bulbs that consume 80% less electricity than old filament bulbs
rubric.note: Drastically cuts household lighting energy consumption.
rubric.keys: led bulbs|80 percent less energy|energy efficient lighting

rubric.point: Highlight that LEDs last up to 25,000 hours, drastically reducing manufacturing waste
Establish a household habit: always switch off lights when exiting an empty room

dangerous: leave lights on all night in empty rooms

sources.name: UJALA Scheme (Energy Efficiency Services Limited - EESL)

cards.title: Harnessing wind and water: Kinetic energy converted to electricity
facts: Wind turbines harness the kinetic energy of air currents to spin an electromagnetic generator.
Hydroelectric plants use the gravitational potential energy of falling water to drive high-speed turbines.
do: Understand that wind and hydro are natural renewable resources that replenish without fuel combustion
India is among the world's top 5 producers of wind energy, with major wind farms in Tamil Nadu and Gujarat
Support clean grid integration: combining wind, hydro, and solar creates balanced 24/7 renewable power
dont: Never assume renewable energy can only come from rooftop solar panels
Never ignore environmental safeguards needed when planning large hydro dams

myths.statement: Wind turbines consume massive amounts of diesel fuel to spin their blades on windy days.
myths.truth: Wind turbines are spun 100% by natural aerodynamic wind lift, consuming zero fossil fuel.

quiz.q: How do wind turbines generate electricity without burning any coal or gas?
options: Wind blows across aerodynamic blades, spinning a shaft connected to an electric generator
quiz.explanation: Aerodynamic lift turns kinetic wind power into mechanical rotation, driving an electromagnetic generator.

situations: Learning about India's renewable energy goals in science class at {at}, {name} explores green grid technologies.
scenario.question: What comprehensive renewable understanding should {name} share?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Explain that wind turbines convert kinetic air movement directly into electricity without emissions
rubric.note: Understands wind energy physics and clean generation.

rubric.point: Highlight that combining solar (daytime) with wind (evening/coastal) and hydro balances the grid
Note India's global leadership with over 180 GW of installed renewable energy capacity
rubric.note: Fosters national pride in clean tech transitions.

cards.title: Lithium-ion battery care: Charging safety, swelling and recycling
facts: Lithium-ion batteries store immense chemical energy; puncturing or crushing them causes violent thermal runaway.
Charging devices on soft beds or under pillows traps heat, severely degrading battery lifespan and risking fires.
do: Charge phones and gadgets on hard, non-flammable surfaces (desks, tiles) with good air ventilation
Stop using and safely isolate any battery that appears bloated, swollen, or smells strange
Send dead batteries exclusively to certified e-waste recyclers to recover valuable lithium, nickel, and cobalt
dont: Never puncture, bend, hammer, or throw batteries into fire or water
Never use cheap, uncertified counterfeit chargers with missing safety voltage regulators

myths.statement: Puncturing a swollen lithium battery with a pin is a great way to let the trapped air out safely.
myths.truth: Puncturing an internal lithium cell creates a violent short-circuit that erupts into an instant, explosive chemical fireball.

quiz.q: What should you do immediately if a phone or laptop battery starts swelling or bulging outward?
options: Disconnect charger immediately, stop using it, place in fire-safe area, and take to a certified technician
quiz.explanation: Swollen batteries indicate dangerous electrolyte breakdown and must be safely retired without puncturing.

situations: While charging a portable gadget at {at}, {name} notices the plastic casing is warping and the battery is visibly swollen.
scenario.question: What is the only safe procedure for {name}?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Unplug the charger immediately and do NOT continue using or charging the device
rubric.note: Cuts off electrical energy supply before thermal runaway.

rubric.point: Place the swollen device on a non-flammable tile surface away from curtains and beds
Do not puncture or squeeze the battery; take it to an authorized electronics repair center

sources.name: Bureau of Indian Standards (Battery Safety IS 16046)

cards.title: Fuel conservation: Carpooling, public transit and walking short trips
facts: Private personal vehicles are responsible for over 40% of urban transportation greenhouse gas emissions.
One fully loaded electric city bus replaces up to 40 personal private cars on congested roads.
do: Walk or ride a bicycle for short errands under 1-2 kilometers rather than asking for car rides
Coordinate carpooling with neighborhood classmates to travel together in a single shared vehicle
Choose metro trains and public buses whenever traveling across the city
dont: Never use a 1.5-tonne petrol car just to travel 500 meters to buy a single packet of milk
Never idle vehicle engines while parked waiting for friends

myths.statement: Taking your own private car alone for every tiny 300-meter errand is a sign of high social status.
myths.truth: Single-occupant car driving drives severe urban gridlock, local air toxicity, and global climate change.

quiz.q: How many private cars can a single full city bus or metro train remove from congested roads?
options: Up to 30 to 40 cars removed from the road
quiz.explanation: Public mass transit dramatically multiplies transport fuel efficiency per passenger-kilometer.

situations: Planning to visit a neighborhood market 800 meters away at {at}, family members consider taking the car.
scenario.question: How can {name} promote green transit?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Suggest walking or riding bicycles together instead of taking the car for an 800-meter trip
rubric.note: Cuts unnecessary fuel consumption and vehicle emissions.
rubric.keys: walk or cycle|short trip|leave car|save fuel

rubric.point: Explain that short cold-engine car trips consume the highest fuel and cause high pollution
rubric.note: Highlights mechanical fuel penalty of short drives.
rubric.keys: short trips waste fuel|cold engine pollution

rubric.point: Enjoy the fresh air, active movement, and zero parking hassles of walking

dangerous: idle engine outside shop for 20 mins

sources.name: Petroleum Conservation Research Association (PCRA Transport Tips)

cards.title: Green buildings: Natural daylighting, cross-ventilation and insulation
facts: Traditional Indian vernacular architecture used courtyard 'jali' screens and high ceilings for natural cooling.
Green buildings (GRIHA / LEED certified) reduce electricity and water consumption by 30% to 50%.
do: Open opposite windows during cool morning and evening hours to create natural cross-ventilation breezes
Use natural daylight during study hours by placing study desks near windows, keeping lights off
Install light-colored reflective roof coatings ('cool roofs') to bounce away scorching summer heat
dont: Never run air conditioners with windows wide open (forces compressors to run continuously at maximum power)
Never rely entirely on artificial lighting during bright daytime hours

myths.statement: A modern building must be completely sealed with black glass windows and have ACs running 24/7.
myths.truth: Sealed glass towers trap immense heat like greenhouses in Indian climates. Natural cross-ventilation is far cooler.

quiz.q: What is the official national green building rating system developed in India by TERI and MNRE?
options: GRIHA (Green Rating for Integrated Habitat Assessment)
quiz.explanation: GRIHA is India's indigenous national green building rating tool assessing sustainability from design to demolition.

situations: Sitting in a dark room with lights on and curtains closed on a bright sunny afternoon at {at}.
scenario.question: How can {name} practice green building principles at home?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Draw back the curtains and open windows to harness natural daylight and fresh air
rubric.keys: natural daylight|open curtains|turn off lights|fresh air

rubric.point: Open opposite doors or windows to create natural cross-ventilation cooling breezes
rubric.note: Replaces power-hungry air conditioning with natural ventilation.

rubric.point: Learn how traditional Indian architecture (courtyards, jalis) cools homes naturally without AC
rubric.note: Connects modern sustainability to indigenous wisdom.

dangerous: turn on all electric lights in broad daylight

sources.name: GRIHA (Green Rating for Integrated Habitat Assessment)

cards.title: Phantom power loads: Standby power waste and smart meters
facts: Appliances left in 'Standby Mode' (TVs, microwaves, chargers, gaming consoles) consume 'vampire power'.
Standby phantom loads account for up to 10% of an average household's total monthly electricity bill.
do: Switch off appliances at the primary wall switch instead of leaving them on remote standby
Unplug laptop and mobile phone chargers when they are not actively charging a connected device
Check your home's digital electricity meter to understand your family's kilowatt-hour (kWh) consumption
dont: Never leave gaming consoles or desktop computers running in sleep mode 24 hours a day
Never leave phone chargers plugged in and switched on with no phone attached

myths.statement: When an appliance is turned off using its remote control, it consumes zero electricity from the wall.
myths.truth: Remote standby keeps internal transformers and sensors energized, silently consuming vampire power 24/7.

quiz.q: What is 'phantom power' or 'vampire load' in household electronics?
options: Electricity consumed by appliances when switched off by remote but still plugged in and on at the wall
quiz.explanation: Vampire loads continuously drain electricity to power standby indicator LEDs and digital clocks.

situations: Leaving the living room at {at}, the television, gaming console, and phone chargers are all plugged in on standby.
scenario.question: How can {name} eliminate phantom energy waste?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Switch off the main power switches on the wall sockets for the TV and gaming console
rubric.note: Cuts off standby vampire power completely.
rubric.keys: switch off at wall|kill phantom load|cut standby power

rubric.point: Unplug idle chargers that continue drawing small electrical currents when not in use
Track monthly electricity meter bills to celebrate reduced kilowatt-hour (kWh) waste

dangerous: leave gaming console on standby 365 days

sources.name: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE Energy Conservation Guide)

cards.title: Biogas technology: Converting organic waste and dung into clean fuel
facts: Anaerobic digestion by methanogenic bacteria transforms animal dung and organic scraps into clean methane gas.
Biogas replaces smoky firewood and coal in rural kitchens, preventing deadly indoor respiratory illness.
do: Understand that biogas digestors convert organic waste into clean cooking gas (methane) and rich organic fertilizer
Support community biogas plants that process village cattle dung and school kitchen food scraps
Use the nutrient-rich digested slurry as a chemical-free organic fertilizer for crops and gardens
dont: Never let untreated cattle dung or sewage pollute village drinking ponds and groundwater
Never inhale concentrated biogas directly from digestor valves (displaces oxygen)

myths.statement: Biogas smells like raw sewage and produces dirty, black soot when burned on a kitchen stove.
myths.truth: Biogas is predominantly methane, burning with a clean, smokeless blue flame identical to LPG.

quiz.q: What natural biological process inside a sealed biogas plant converts organic waste into methane gas?
options: Anaerobic digestion (fermentation by bacteria in the absence of oxygen)
quiz.explanation: Methanogenic bacteria break down complex organic polymers in oxygen-free tanks to produce methane.

situations: Visiting a rural farm or school eco-project at {at}, {name} sees a Gobar Gas / Biogas digestor dome.
scenario.question: What circular economy benefits should {name} explain?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: The digestor turns cattle dung and organic waste into clean, smokeless methane cooking gas
The leftover digested slurry serves as a superior, chemical-free organic fertilizer for soil
Biogas eliminates indoor smoke from burning firewood, protecting women's and children's lungs

dangerous: dump raw dung in drinking well

sources.name: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (National Bioenergy Programme)

cards.title: How plastic recycling works: Shredding, melting and circular textiles
facts: Mechanical recycling washes, shreds, and melts clean PET plastic bottles into reusable resin pellets.
Recycled PET (rPET) pellets are extruded into fine polyester yarn used for sports jerseys, backpacks, and ropes.
do: Rinse and crush empty plastic bottles before disposing of them in dry recyclable waste bins
Support circular products manufactured from verified post-consumer recycled plastic (rPET)
Understand that dirty, contaminated plastic cannot be recycled and ends up incinerated or in landfills
dont: Never throw half-full milk packets or sticky food containers into dry paper recycling bins
Never mix greasy food waste with clean plastic packaging

myths.statement: All types of plastic can be melted and remelted infinite times without ever degrading in quality.
myths.truth: Plastic polymers degrade with each thermal recycling cycle (downcycling). Reducing plastic use is always primary.

quiz.q: What high-performance product can clean recycled PET plastic drink bottles be turned into?
options: Recycled polyester textile yarn for sports jerseys and jackets
quiz.explanation: Clean PET bottles are shredded into flakes, melted, and spun into polyester textile fibers.

situations: Finishing a bottle of water or juice at {at}, {name} prepares to discard the plastic container.
scenario.question: How should {name} prep the bottle for high-grade mechanical recycling?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Empty any remaining liquid, rinse lightly, remove cap, and crush the bottle flat
rubric.note: Prevents contamination and saves transport volume.
rubric.keys: rinse bottle|crush flat|dry waste bin|clean plastic

rubric.point: Deposit it in the blue 'Dry Recyclable Waste' bin for formal kabadiwala collection
rubric.note: Routes container into circular industrial recycling.

rubric.point: Remember that reducing and refusing single-use plastic is always superior to recycling
rubric.note: Upholds the waste hierarchy (Reduce > Reuse > Recycle).

dangerous: throw half-full sticky bottle in paper bin

sources.name: Central Pollution Control Board (Plastic Waste Management Division)

cards.title: RO water purifiers: Harvesting and reusing reject water
facts: Household Reverse Osmosis (RO) purifiers reject 3 to 4 litres of water for every 1 litre of purified drinking water.
Draining RO reject water straight into sewage pipes wastes over 60 litres of clean municipal water per home daily.
do: Route the RO reject wastewater pipe into a clean storage bucket or drum in your kitchen
Use RO reject water for floor mopping, washing dirty utensils, cleaning balconies, or car washing
Water sturdy garden plants with reject water (if Total Dissolved Solids / TDS is not excessively salty)
dont: Never let the RO reject pipe drain directly down the kitchen sink drainpipe into sewer lines
Never drink RO reject water (it contains concentrated minerals and dissolved salts)

myths.statement: Reject water from household RO purifiers is toxic poisonous chemical waste that cannot be used for anything.
myths.truth: RO reject water is simply concentrated mineral tap water; it is perfectly suited for mopping, washing, and cleaning.

quiz.q: For every 1 litre of pure drinking water produced, approximately how much wastewater does a home RO purifier discard?
options: About 3 to 4 litres of reject water discarded down the drain
quiz.explanation: RO membrane technology discards 75% of incoming water to wash concentrated salts away from membranes.

situations: In the kitchen at {at}, {name} notices the thin white pipe of the RO purifier gushing water straight into the sink drain.
scenario.question: What water-saving intervention should {name} make?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Place a clean bucket under the RO reject pipe to capture the discarded water
rubric.note: Harvests dozens of litres of usable water daily.
rubric.keys: capture ro reject water|bucket under pipe|harvest wastewater

rubric.point: Use the harvested reject water for washing utensils, mopping floors, or flushing toilets
rubric.note: Replaces fresh municipal water for non-potable cleaning chores.

rubric.point: Explain to family that throwing RO reject water down the drain wastes 60 litres daily

dangerous: let pipe run down sink drain 24/7

sources.name: Central Ground Water Board (Water Conservation Guidelines)

cards.title: Green tech careers: Solar engineers, EV designers and sustainability experts
facts: The global transition to net-zero carbon is creating millions of high-growth 'green collar' careers.
Green industries span renewable energy engineering, energy auditing, circular design, and environmental law.
do: Explore technical engineering degrees: Renewable Energy Engineering, Electrical & Battery Tech, or Environmental Science
Develop skills in environmental impact assessment (EIA), ESG compliance, and energy simulation software
Look into corporate sustainability: companies hire sustainability managers to decarbonize supply chains
dont: Never assume that caring for the planet means you can only volunteer for zero pay
Never view green jobs as a niche charity sector; it is the dominant economic growth sector of this century

myths.statement: Careers in renewable energy and environment only offer low-paying volunteer jobs with no future.
myths.truth: Solar technology, electric mobility, and grid analytics are multi-trillion-dollar industries hiring top engineers and leaders.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a high-growth 'green collar' career contributing to clean technology?
options: Battery Management System (BMS) Engineer / Renewable Grid Specialist
quiz.explanation: EV battery design and renewable grid integration are among the fastest-growing engineering specialties globally.

situations: A student in Class 11 at {at} loves physics and technology and wants a career that helps fight climate change.
scenario.question: How can {name} introduce them to green tech pathways?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Highlight cutting-edge fields: Electric Vehicle Battery Engineering, Solar PV Architecture, and Smart Grids
rubric.note: Connects technology interest with climate solutions.
rubric.keys: ev battery engineering|solar pv|smart grids|renewable energy

rubric.point: Discuss emerging roles: ESG Sustainability Consultant, Environmental Law, and Carbon Accounting
Focus on strong fundamentals in mathematics, physics, and computer simulation modeling

push them into declining fossil fuel careers

cards.title: Understanding your carbon footprint: Food, travel and energy choices
facts: A 'carbon footprint' is the total greenhouse gases (measured in kg of CO2 equivalent) generated by your daily actions.
Major contributors to personal carbon footprints are electricity use, personal transport, food choices, and material goods.
do: Calculate your lifestyle carbon footprint using free online student carbon calculators
Reduce travel footprint: walk, cycle, carpool, and prefer train travel over domestic flights where feasible
Reduce food footprint: eat local seasonal produce and prevent plate food waste from rotting in landfills
dont: Never believe that individual conservation actions are useless; collective youth habits shift entire markets
Never waste electricity and food thinking nature will replenish resources automatically

myths.statement: Your personal carbon footprint is fixed at birth and cannot be altered by your daily lifestyle choices.
myths.truth: Switching to cycling, eating local produce, and turning off appliances can cut your personal footprint by over 40%

quiz.q: Which of the following personal habits creates the largest reduction in an individual's carbon footprint?
options: Walking/cycling for short trips, cutting food waste, and using energy-efficient appliances
quiz.explanation: Active mobility, food waste elimination, and electrical efficiency directly slash greenhouse emissions.

situations: In environmental science class at {at}, {name} is learning about personal carbon footprints.
scenario.question: How can {name} turn this knowledge into a practical daily action plan?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Audit personal daily habits: electricity use, short errand transport, and plate food waste
rubric.note: Builds measurable personal awareness of emissions.
rubric.keys: audit daily habits|transport choices|food waste|electricity use

rubric.point: Adopt active sustainable shifts: use cycles for local trips, switch off idle appliances, eat local food
rubric.note: Translates awareness into direct carbon reductions.
rubric.keys: cycle local trips|switch off appliances|eat local food

rubric.point: Encourage family and school to track energy conservation together for collective impact
rubric.note: Amplifies individual impact to community scale.

sources.name: Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment - NITI Aayog)

cards.title: Right to Repair: Combating planned obsolescence in electronics
facts: 'Planned obsolescence' is when manufacturers intentionally design gadgets to be unrepairable, forcing new purchases.
The Right to Repair framework empowers consumers to access spare parts, repair manuals, and third-party repair services.
do: Support the Right to Repair movement: buy electronics from brands that provide modular parts and repair guides
Learn basic maintenance skills: replacing laptop batteries, cleaning fan dust, or changing phone screens
Choose repair over premature replacement whenever an appliance or gadget malfunctions
dont: Never buy glued-together gadgets designed to be thrown away when a single sub-component fails
Never discard electronics with simple fixable loose wires or worn-out batteries

myths.statement: Manufacturers make phones impossible to repair at local shops purely for your safety.
myths.truth: Companies restrict repair manuals and glue batteries to force consumers into buying costly new upgrades every 2 years.

quiz.q: What is the objective of the Government of India's 'Right to Repair' portal (righttorepairindia.gov.in)?
options: To ensure consumers and local repairers can access genuine spare parts, diagnostic tools, and manuals
quiz.explanation: The Right to Repair portal holds manufacturers accountable for providing repair documentation and spare parts.

situations: A family laptop at {at} has a degraded battery that only lasts 15 minutes, and a salesman urges buying a new ₹60,000 laptop.
scenario.question: How can {name} apply Right to Repair principles?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Check if the battery can be replaced by a local certified technician for a fraction of the cost
rubric.note: Restores device functionality without expensive replacement.
rubric.keys: replace battery|repair laptop|fraction of cost|right to repair

rubric.point: Explain that throwing away an entire working laptop for a worn battery generates toxic e-waste
rubric.note: Highlights ecological impact of planned obsolescence.

rubric.point: Check the Department of Consumer Affairs Right to Repair portal for authorized repair options

dangerous: buy new laptop for simple dead battery

sources.name: Department of Consumer Affairs (Right to Repair India Portal)

cards.title: Solar thermal energy: Solar water heaters and solar cookers
facts: Solar thermal systems convert sunlight directly into heat energy without generating electricity first.
A rooftop solar water heater replaces electric geysers, saving over 1,500 units of electricity per household annually.
do: Understand that solar water heaters use black evacuated glass tubes to absorb solar infrared heat directly into water
Solar box cookers use mirrors and glass tops to slow-cook rice, dal, and vegetables with zero gas or firewood
Support rooftop solar water heating in residential buildings and school hostels to cut peak winter electricity demands
dont: Never break or shatter evacuated solar glass tubes (maintain vacuum insulation)
Never touch piping near solar collectors without testing (water reaches scalding 80°C temperatures)

myths.statement: Solar water heaters need electric heaters running underneath them to warm water on sunny winter days.
myths.truth: Evacuated vacuum tubes absorb solar infrared radiation so efficiently that water boils naturally even in cold winter air.

quiz.q: How much electricity can a 100-litre domestic rooftop solar water heater save in a year?
options: Approximately 1,500 kWh of electricity saved annually
quiz.explanation: Replacing electric resistance immersion geysers with solar thermal saves massive amounts of coal-fired grid power.

situations: Looking at an evacuated tube solar water heater on a building terrace at {at}, {name} explains how it works.
scenario.question: What thermal energy facts should {name} share?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Solar thermal collectors absorb infrared sunlight directly into water tubes with zero electricity used
rubric.keys: solar thermal|absorbs heat directly|no electricity used|evacuated tubes

rubric.point: Rooftop solar water heaters save over 1,500 units of electricity per family each year
rubric.note: Demonstrates massive energy and cost savings.
rubric.keys: saves 1500 units electricity|cuts power bills|replaces geyser

rubric.point: Solar box cookers can bake and slow-cook meals using trapped greenhouse solar heat

cards.title: The digital energy footprint: Data centers, video streaming and cloud storage
facts: The internet and massive hyperscale data centers consume over 2% of the entire world's electricity.
Streaming 4K video, storing thousands of unwanted cloud photos, and spam emails consume continuous server power.
do: Delete unwanted duplicate photos, massive unused cloud backup files, and unsubscribe from spam emails
Lower video streaming resolution to 720p or 1080p when watching on small mobile phone screens (4K is invisible on tiny screens)
Use local offline downloads over Wi-Fi instead of repeatedly streaming the same music tracks on cellular data
dont: Never leave video streams running in the background when nobody is watching the screen
Never hoard thousands of junk unread promotional emails on cloud servers

myths.statement: Storing 50,000 unneeded blurry photos in the cloud consumes zero electricity because the cloud is in the sky.
myths.truth: The 'cloud' is thousands of massive warehouse data centers packed with servers cooled by enormous air conditioners 24/7.

quiz.q: Where does data stored in the 'cloud' actually live in the physical world?
options: Inside massive physical data center warehouses packed with servers running on electricity 24/7
quiz.explanation: Cloud data requires continuous physical server power and massive chilling cooling systems.

situations: Organizing their digital smartphone at {at}, {name} notices 15,000 duplicate blurry photos and 3,000 unread spam emails.
scenario.question: How can {name} practice digital environmental hygiene?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Delete duplicate blurry photos and empty the trash folder to free up cloud server storage
rubric.note: Reduces physical server storage and cooling power requirements.
rubric.keys: clean cloud storage|delete duplicate photos|digital cleanup

rubric.point: Unsubscribe from junk marketing email lists and delete old promotional messages
rubric.note: Stops ongoing data center processing loops.

rubric.point: Stream video at 1080p rather than 4K on small phone screens where quality difference is invisible
rubric.note: Cuts data transfer bandwidth and transmission energy.

sources.name: International Energy Agency (Data Centres and Energy Use)

cards.title: Busting renewable energy myths: Storage, reliability and recycling
facts: Modern grid-scale battery storage and pumped-hydro provide continuous power when the sun sets or wind calms.
Solar panels pay back the energy used to manufacture them within 1 to 2 years, producing clean power for 25+ years.
do: Understand that renewable energy is now the cheapest source of new electricity generation in history
Recognize that batteries, solar panels, and wind turbine components are recyclable in certified facilities
Support decentralized microgrids that bring clean, reliable solar electricity to remote rural communities
dont: Never believe that the grid will crash if solar power exceeds 20% (modern smart inverters stabilize grids)
Never believe that renewable energy technology causes more pollution than coal power

myths.statement: Renewable energy is so expensive that only rich Western countries can afford solar and wind power.
myths.truth: Solar electricity costs have plunged by over 85% in the last decade; solar is now the cheapest electricity in India.

quiz.q: How quickly does a modern solar photovoltaic panel generate back all the energy used to manufacture it?
options: Within 1 to 2 years of operation, after which it produces clean net-positive power for 25+ years
quiz.explanation: Solar panels have an Energy Payback Time (EPBT) of just 1-2 years, generating clean energy for decades thereafter.

situations: In a classroom debate at {at}, an opponent claims solar energy is too unreliable and expensive to replace coal.
scenario.question: How should {name} debunk this myth with scientific data?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Present data showing that solar energy is now the lowest-cost source of new electricity in India
rubric.keys: solar is cheapest electricity|costs plunged 85%|economic reality

rubric.point: Explain that combining solar with wind, pumped hydro, and grid battery storage ensures 24/7 reliability
rubric.note: Solves intermittency with modern grid architecture.
rubric.keys: grid battery storage|pumped hydro|wind mix|24/7 reliability

rubric.point: Point out that over 90% of materials in solar panels (glass, aluminum, silicon) can be recycled

dangerous: agree that coal must burn forever
